title.narrative: DEC Phase 2: Emergency Appeal Rohingya Refugees. CI Appeal EA32/2017

description.narrative: Since the submission of the Phase 1 Plan and the initiation of the planned activities, the overall situation in the targeted areas has not changed. The number of refugees arriving in Bangladesh has been decreasing over the past months, with more than 24,000 in November, more than 3,000 in December and 1,888 in January 2018. The condition in the camps remains poor, as high population density has led to the exhaustion of initially installed temporary services, particularly sanitation, and there has been widespread environmental destruction of plants and trees, including roots, which have been taken for fuel. A lack of site planning in the initial stages of this crisis has created congested and dense camp layouts, that are lacking protection elements such as street lighting, and also strong shelters and accessible pathways. A Joint Response Plan (JRP) has been developed and shared with local authorities with plans detailed per sector, the current Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) is due to finish in February 2018. Across all sectors there has been a noted shift towards resilience activities focused on the upcoming rainy/ cyclone season. For example, for shelter/NFI the focus is shifting to shelter upgrade kits to help improve resilience to the upcoming rainy/ cyclone season, and immediate site improvements that will help minimise the risk of flooding and landslides. CAFOD’s partner Caritas Bangladesh will be working with 4 Maghi’s (camp areas of approximately 100 HHs, each with their own leader) in Palong Khali (400 households/ 2,000 individuals) to deliver the site development activities. As the project will be working at a small scale, all household vulnerability data will be analysed ahead of project activities and visits will be made to homes of the most vulnerable as part of the consultation and activity planning, to share information and gather community feedback.
